title: TESCO Bill Calculator 2026 (Latest Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your TESCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. Protected TESCO units explained.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the TESCO per unit rate in 2026?
p: TESCO here is the Tribal Electric Supply Company Limited of Peshawar, not the British supermarket. It is the smallest of the ex-WAPDA distribution companies, created to serve the former tribal agencies and frontier regions that are now the merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Its domestic consumers are billed on the uniform A-1 tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026, so the per unit rate is the national slab rate: an unprotected home using 200 units pays Rs 28.91 on every unit.

Many homes in TESCO's area use little electricity for most of the year, which keeps them in the protected or lifeline categories at much lower rates. The examples below show the same month billed both ways so you can see what protection is worth.

sections.h2: Is the TESCO tariff different from PESCO's?
p: No. PESCO serves the settled districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Peshawar, Mardan, Swat, Kohat, Bannu, D.I. Khan and the rest, while TESCO serves the merged districts: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan, together with the former frontier regions attached to them. Both bill the same uniform domestic slabs and the same fixed charge per kW, and both print the NEPRA-notified FPA for the month.

What does differ in TESCO's area is the metering history. Where meters were installed recently or readings are irregular, a single bill may cover more than a month of use and land in a higher slab than a normal month would. The overbilling check shows what a long reading cycle does to the slab.

sections.h2: What does a protected TESCO consumer pay?
p: A home is protected when all of its last 6 bills were at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW. Protected bills are worked out slab-wise at two low rates, so 200 protected units cost Rs 2,355 in energy charge, against Rs 5,782 for the same units billed unprotected. The difference is larger than every other line on the bill put together.

One month over the limit, whatever the cause, moves the home to unprotected rates for the next 6 bills. If a heater or a new fan pushes winter or summer use close to the limit, the protected check on the main bill calculator shows how much room is left.

sections.h2: TESCO bill check: estimate here, confirm on the printed bill
p: This page estimates a TESCO bill from the units and category you enter. It cannot see your account, arrears, the exact FPA or any local charge. The printed bill, with the reference number and due date, is available from TESCO and through the online bill lookup by reference number; use that to pay and this page to understand the lines.

The full electricity bill calculator for Pakistan explains the slabs and the protected check in more depth; the maths is the same. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for TESCO.

faq.q: How do I get a TESCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from your bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 200 units the estimate is Rs 8,548, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the TESCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches: Rs 28.91 per unit for an unprotected home using 200 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab, including the protected and lifeline rates.

faq.q: What is the TESCO tariff for 2026?
faq.a: The uniform A-1 domestic tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: lifeline slabs up to 100 units, protected slabs up to 200 units, unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700 and an open-ended top slab; connections of 5 kW and above are billed on ToU rates.

The merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, formerly FATA: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan, with the former frontier regions. The settled districts of the province, including Peshawar itself, are PESCO.

faq.q: How do I check my TESCO bill online?
faq.a: Through TESCO's online bill lookup by the reference number printed on the bill, which shows the current bill, due date and payment status. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Is TESCO the same as the UK supermarket Tesco?
faq.a: No. The Pakistani TESCO is the Tribal Electric Supply Company Limited, a NEPRA-licensed electricity distributor based in Peshawar. This page is about its electricity bills.

faq.q: Why is my TESCO bill higher than this estimate?
faq.a: Usually the month's FPA, arrears or a late-payment surcharge, or a bill that covers more than a month of readings. Replace the pre-filled FPA with your bill's in the advanced fields; for a long reading period use the overbilling check.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: TESCO, the Tribal Electric Supply Company Limited, is the ex-WAPDA distribution company for the merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (the former FATA), run from WAPDA House on Shami Road in Peshawar; it bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026.
The TESCO per unit rate for an unprotected home using 200 units is Rs 28.91 on every unit, giving Rs 5,782 in energy charges before the fixed charge, surcharges and GST.
A TESCO consumer whose last 6 bills were all at or under 200 units is billed slab-wise at the protected rates; the second example below shows how much lower that makes the same month.
The slab rates on a TESCO bill are identical to those on a PESCO bill from Peshawar or Mardan; the two companies differ only in the area they serve, because NEPRA sets one FPA for both.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,481 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Searching for the supermarket. TESCO on a Pakistani bill is the Tribal Electric Supply Company of Peshawar; its tariff is the NEPRA domestic tariff, not a retail price list.

Expecting a lower tribal-area rate. The slab rates are uniform across Pakistan; the lower bills in the merged districts come from the protected and lifeline categories, which depend on how many units the home uses.
Ticking protected after one high month. Protection needs all of the last 6 bills at or under 200 units.
Paying a bill for a long reading period as if it were one month. More than a month of units on one bill can land in a higher slab; run it through the overbilling check first.

fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

content.answer: A TESCO home in the merged districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa using 200 units a month as an unprotected consumer on a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 8,548: Rs 5,782 energy charge at Rs 28.91 per unit plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. TESCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges + FPA + GST.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the bill
